source.title: AlignSAE: Concept-Aligned Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Minglai Yang; Xin-Yu Guo; Zheng-Liang Shi; Jin-He Bi; Steven Bethard; Mihai Surdeanu; Liangming Pan

record.tranche_reason: The study uses concept-slot binding as a different diagnostic measure to investigate whether internal representational progress precedes delayed generalization in a synthetic two-hop reasoning task.
record.gate_note: The relevant results are the reported two-hop validation-accuracy transition and concept-slot binding measurements across training. The study does not report a training-set-size sweep. Other SAE alignment, steering, and swap results do not bear on the claim versions and are omitted.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own training-dynamics results on a new setting: GPT-2 124M fine-tuned on a synthetic natural-language two-hop relational task. Validation accuracy stays low, then jumps late. An SAE-based concept–slot binding measure is tracked against it. These results bear on V1 (delayed generalization) and V2 (a progress measure anticipating the jump). T3 fits better than T2 because the setting, not just the method, differs from the algorithmic originals.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right. The authors say the two-hop model shows grokking-like dynamics. They read early-saturating binding accuracy and later validation gains as 'hidden' progress (knowing before showing). They also describe grokking as a phase transition from entangled to clean step-wise slot bindings, with epoch 10 diffuse and epoch 40 perfectly diagonal.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a natural-language synthetic two-hop relational reasoning task and measures concept-slot binding with an AlignSAE, rather than the original algorithmic-dataset setup and its training/test accuracy and dataset-size measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The binding measurements differ by prediction step (Token 1 versus Token 2) at epoch 10; the reported validation-accuracy transition is shown over training epochs.
record.problems: The grokking analysis is on a single GPT-2 model and a synthetic two-hop task. The relevant accuracy curves are presented in figures without numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The study does not report training accuracy for this analysis or vary the training-set size.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted other reported AlignSAE results, including one-hop alignment and swap interventions, because they do not measure grokking dynamics or the mechanisms named in the tested versions.

untested.parts: Small algorithmic datasets as such (the task is templated natural-language relational reasoning). Training accuracy saturating before the jump. A jump from chance to near-perfect (levels not readable). Dependence of the delay on training-set size (only a fixed 4,000/4,000 split).
Removal of memorizing components. Whether the measure tracks the actual generalizing circuit rather than a supervised probe readout. Any Fourier-style or circuit-level mechanism.

missing.what: t-SNE of supervised slot activations across epochs: no structure at epoch 5, clusters forming by 25, clean separation by 100. This bears on the gradual timing of the binding measure.
Per-hop validation accuracy curves (Token 1 vs Token 2) and training vs validation loss across training

record.verdict_notes: The grokking analysis is a side probe in an SAE-methods paper: one model, one run, figure-only curves, no uncertainty. The binding measure comes from an SAE explicitly supervised to map relation labels to slots. The relations are named in the query text, so high diagonal accuracy may reflect decodability of input relation identity rather than formation of the generalizing circuit. The two lines of evidence also don't line up cleanly: Fig. 9 says binding saturates early, while Fig. 8 calls epoch 10 pre-grokking with only 38.4%/69.5% binding. The SAE results on swaps, MIG and FB15K do not bear on any version.

versions.untested_parts: The study reports delayed validation accuracy on its two-hop task, but does not report that training accuracy reaches perfect accuracy while test accuracy stays at chance, nor whether the delay grows as the training set shrinks.

It measures concept-slot binding over training and its timing relative to validation accuracy. It does not measure removal of memorizing components or establish that the binding measure is continuous progress in the generalizing circuit.

rows.value: figure only; described as remaining low for many epochs before a sharp transition
rows.note: The text explicitly describes delayed validation improvement, but does not give numerical accuracy values for the curve.
rows.check: Figure-only. The text says validation accuracy 'remains low for many epochs before a sharp transition'. Training accuracy is not shown, only training loss, which 'decreases smoothly'. So saturation of training accuracy before the jump is not established, and the start and end levels can't be read. Unlinked from V2: a validation curve alone is not a progress measure.

rows.subject: GPT-2
rows.operation_detail: Track concept-slot diagonal accuracy during training.
rows.value: figure only; described as climbing rapidly and saturating before validation accuracy improves
rows.note: The authors interpret this earlier saturation as hidden representational progress preceding the validation-accuracy transition.
rows.check: Figure-only. Diagonal accuracy 'climbs rapidly and saturates early' while validation accuracy jumps later (Fig. 9). The measure is the readout of a supervised SAE trained to bind relation labels to slots. It may index linear decodability of the relation named in the query rather than the generalizing circuit.

rows.subject: GPT-2
rows.operation_detail: Measure relation-to-slot diagonal accuracy at the intermediate-entity prediction step.
rows.note: At this pre-grokking checkpoint, binding is not yet perfectly diagonal.
rows.check: 38.4% diagonal accuracy at epoch 10 (Token 1) is a value of the binding measure itself, not a test of whether it anticipates the jump. Its timing relative to the validation jump is not given numerically. It also sits awkwardly with Fig. 9's claim that binding saturates early, since the text calls epoch 10 'pre-grokking' with diffuse binding.
